You need generative or LLM-judged citation attribution rather than deterministic embedding-similarity matching — AgriIR deliberately uses a fixed threshold, not model reasoning Your answer sentences are not segmentable by a sentence tokenizer (e.g. bullet lists or tables) — the method operates per-sentence Your source pool is not chunked into two-level (ij) DB/WEB indices, so the [DB_ij]/[WEB_ij] token scheme cannot address sources http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stage 6 of the AgriIR pipeline deterministically inserts inline citations ([DB_ij] / [WEB_ij]) into a synthesized answer by matching each sentence against retrieved source chunks with a Sentence Transformer and keeping matches whose cosine similarity is ≥ 0.75. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-21324-2_37
skills.summary: Stage 6 of the AgriIR pipeline deterministically inserts inline citations ([DB_ij] / [WEB_ij]) into a synthesized answer by matching each sentence against retrieved source chunks with a Sentence Transformer and keeping matches whose cosine similarity is ≥ 0.75.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need generative or LLM-judged citation attribution rather than deterministic embedding-similarity matching — AgriIR deliberately uses a fixed threshold, not model reasoning Your answer sentences are not segmentable by a sentence tokenizer (e.g. bullet lists or tables) — the method operates per-sentence Your source pool is not chunked into two-level (ij) DB/WEB indices, so the [DB_ij]/[WEB_ij] token scheme cannot address sources

skills.description: Use when a batch annotation run over an image set has completed and you need per-dataset efficiency metrics (success rate, avg iterations, tokens per success) from the output records.
skills.name: annotation-operational-statistics-aggregation
skills.search_text: annotation-operational-statistics-aggregation Use when a batch annotation run over an image set has completed and you need per-dataset efficiency metrics (success rate, avg iterations, tokens per success) from the output records. You only have single-pass annotation outputs with no iteration or is_successful fields — the iteration/token-per-success metrics cannot be computed. The goal is quality/accuracy evaluation of the annotations (e.g., grounding accuracy vs. multimodal LLMs) rather than operational efficiency of the loop. The run used a different acceptance threshold (τ) or max_iter than 0.9/5, making direct comparison to the reported 91.8%/89.2% figures invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Aggregates per-image records from an automated annotation loop (AutoVQA-G) into operational statistics — success rate, average iterations per success, and token cost per success — per dataset, to quantify annotation efficiency on Visual7W and Viz Wiz. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11462754
skills.summary: Aggregates per-image records from an automated annotation loop (AutoVQA-G) into operational statistics — success rate, average iterations per success, and token cost per success — per dataset, to quantify annotation efficiency on Visual7W and Viz Wiz.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have single-pass annotation outputs with no iteration or is_successful fields — the iteration/token-per-success metrics cannot be computed. The goal is quality/accuracy evaluation of the annotations (e.g., grounding accuracy vs. multimodal LLMs) rather than operational efficiency of the loop. The run used a different acceptance threshold (τ) or max_iter than 0.9/5, making direct comparison to the reported 91.8%/89.2% figures invalid.

skills.description: Use when a sparse-reward RL pipeline needs symbolic expert demonstration data to fine-tune a language-model action predictor, and the environment is a discrete grid world (e.g. MiniGrid 4x4/8x8 UnlockPickup) representable as a transition graph.
skills.name: astar-optimal-trajectory-synthesis
skills.search_text: astar-optimal-trajectory-synthesis Use when a sparse-reward RL pipeline needs symbolic expert demonstration data to fine-tune a language-model action predictor, and the environment is a discrete grid world (e.g. MiniGrid 4x4/8x8 UnlockPickup) representable as a transition graph. The task environment is not a discrete grid world representable as a transition graph over cell states and actions (A* over a Manhattan heuristic will not yield meaningful optimal trajectories). The goal is to evaluate the full ULPS policy against RL baselines (Unguided PPO, Linear Decay, Q-Learning, DQN) rather than to generate fine-tuning data for the action predictor. Environment dynamics are stochastic or continuous, so a single optimal symbolic trajectory per start-goal pair is not well defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Synthesizes optimal symbolic state-action trajectories for the MiniGrid-UnlockPickup environment using an A* oracle with a Manhattan distance heuristic, and converts them into textual prompts used to fine-tune a bert-base-uncased next-action predictor. This is the data-generation stage of ULPS that replaces costly environment interactions with oracle-derived supervision. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536354
skills.summary: Synthesizes optimal symbolic state-action trajectories for the MiniGrid-UnlockPickup environment using an A* oracle with a Manhattan distance heuristic, and converts them into textual prompts used to fine-tune a bert-base-uncased next-action predictor. This is the data-generation stage of ULPS that replaces costly environment interactions with oracle-derived supervision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task environment is not a discrete grid world representable as a transition graph over cell states and actions (A* over a Manhattan heuristic will not yield meaningful optimal trajectories). The goal is to evaluate the full ULPS policy against RL baselines (Unguided PPO, Linear Decay, Q-Learning, DQN) rather than to generate fine-tuning data for the action predictor. Environment dynamics are stochastic or continuous, so a single optimal symbolic trajectory per start-goal pair is not well defined.

skills.description: Use when you have an image-question pair (e.g., ScienceQA) and a pretrained multimodal LLM that exposes cross-attention maps, and you need to generate a negatively perturbed image whose masked regions correspond to the question-relevant high-attention areas.
skills.name: attention-map-upsampling-and-gaussian-smoothing
skills.search_text: attention-map-upsampling-and-gaussian-smoothing Use when you have an image-question pair (e.g., ScienceQA) and a pretrained multimodal LLM that exposes cross-attention maps, and you need to generate a negatively perturbed image whose masked regions correspond to the question-relevant high-attention areas. The input is text-only (no image tokens), so no cross-attention saliency over visual regions can be aggregated and upsampled. The goal is the SVD steering-vector extraction or layer-wise injection step of VSSD (governed by hyperparameters alpha/beta), not the construction of the perturbed image itself. The downstream model does not expose cross-attention maps over image tokens, since the mask cannot be derived without them. Constructs VSSD's negatively perturbed semantic image samples (I_r) by turning a multimodal LLM's cross-attention maps over image tokens into a denoised, top-k-thresholded binary mask that is applied to the original ScienceQA image. This captures the task-sensitive visual regions the teacher model attends to, feeding the saliency-guided distillation pipeline. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11463006
skills.summary: Constructs VSSD's negatively perturbed semantic image samples (I_r) by turning a multimodal LLM's cross-attention maps over image tokens into a denoised, top-k-thresholded binary mask that is applied to the original ScienceQA image. This captures the task-sensitive visual regions the teacher model attends to, feeding the saliency-guided distillation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is text-only (no image tokens), so no cross-attention saliency over visual regions can be aggregated and upsampled. The goal is the SVD steering-vector extraction or layer-wise injection step of VSSD (governed by hyperparameters alpha/beta), not the construction of the perturbed image itself. The downstream model does not expose cross-attention maps over image tokens, since the mask cannot be derived without them.

skills.description: Use when comparing probabilistic action predictors (e.g., an LLM policy vs. uncalibrated LLM, unguided RL, or prior work) and you need discrimination plus calibration metrics (ECE, Brier Score, AUC-ROC) consolidated into a comparison table.
skills.name: auc-roc-discrimination-analysis
skills.search_text: auc-roc-discrimination-analysis Use when comparing probabilistic action predictors (e.g., an LLM policy vs. uncalibrated LLM, unguided RL, or prior work) and you need discrimination plus calibration metrics (ECE, Brier Score, AUC-ROC) consolidated into a comparison table. When only a single model's point-estimate accuracy is needed with no probabilistic calibration or ranking comparison When the environment/task is not MiniGrid-UnlockPickup-style sparse-reward RL with binary per-episode success outcomes, since the discrimination metric is defined over binary episode outcomes When you cannot produce predicted action probabilities (e.g., a deterministic policy without confidence scores), as ECE/Brier/AUC-ROC all require calibrated probability outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes Discrimination Analysis (AUC-ROC) alongside accuracy, 10-bin Expected Calibration Error, and Brier Score to evaluate whether a fine-tuned BERT action predictor produces better-calibrated probabilistic predictions than prior/baseline models in the ULPS MiniGrid-UnlockPickup setting. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536354
skills.summary: Computes Discrimination Analysis (AUC-ROC) alongside accuracy, 10-bin Expected Calibration Error, and Brier Score to evaluate whether a fine-tuned BERT action predictor produces better-calibrated probabilistic predictions than prior/baseline models in the ULPS MiniGrid-UnlockPickup setting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single model's point-estimate accuracy is needed with no probabilistic calibration or ranking comparison When the environment/task is not MiniGrid-UnlockPickup-style sparse-reward RL with binary per-episode success outcomes, since the discrimination metric is defined over binary episode outcomes When you cannot produce predicted action probabilities (e.g., a deterministic policy without confidence scores), as ECE/Brier/AUC-ROC all require calibrated probability outputs

skills.search_text: audio-toolchain-orchestration Use when a task requires transforming an uploaded speech recording's emotional tone (e.g. angry to happy) while keeping the speaker's voice, needing chained recognition-transcription-editing-resynthesis steps rather than a single tool. skills.description: Use when a constrained-generation LLM pipeline needs a scalable disk-backed fact index over a very large KB (e.g., Wikidata), and in-memory prefix trees are infeasible due to hardware memory limits.
skills.name: b-tree-prefix-lookup-tuning
skills.search_text: b-tree-prefix-lookup-tuning Use when a constrained-generation LLM pipeline needs a scalable disk-backed fact index over a very large KB (e.g., Wikidata), and in-memory prefix trees are infeasible due to hardware memory limits. The knowledge base is small enough to fit an in-memory prefix tree — the article uses a 31k-facts in-memory tree via try_refactx.ipynb instead of the disk-backed PostgreSQL index. The workflow uses a retriever or auxiliary retrieval model rather than constrained generation over a pre-built fact index — ReFactX is explicitly positioned as an alternative to pipeline-based solutions. The task is inference-time constrained generation over an already-built index rather than index construction and lookup tuning. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs and persists a PostgreSQL-backed prefix-tree index over verbalized, tokenized knowledge-base facts (ReFactX: up to 800M Wikidata facts), using batched ingestion, Pickle subtree packing, single-leaf compression, and a B-Tree index on the Prefix column so per-decoding-step prefix-match lookups add only ~1% latency. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-09527-5_16
skills.summary: Constructs and persists a PostgreSQL-backed prefix-tree index over verbalized, tokenized knowledge-base facts (ReFactX: up to 800M Wikidata facts), using batched ingestion, Pickle subtree packing, single-leaf compression, and a B-Tree index on the Prefix column so per-decoding-step prefix-match lookups add only ~1% latency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The knowledge base is small enough to fit an in-memory prefix tree — the article uses a 31k-facts in-memory tree via try_refactx.ipynb instead of the disk-backed PostgreSQL index. The workflow uses a retriever or auxiliary retrieval model rather than constrained generation over a pre-built fact index — ReFactX is explicitly positioned as an alternative to pipeline-based solutions. The task is inference-time constrained generation over an already-built index rather than index construction and lookup tuning.

skills.search_text: baseline-ablation-comparison-tables Use when a paper reports a two-stage multimodal CoT evaluation comparing an ablation setting (e.g., PI vs BKG images) against a baseline across model sizes, and the numbers must be reproduced into a comparison table. The evaluation is single-stage (direct QCM→A) with no rationale generation, so RougeL cannot be computed. The task requires hyperparameter tuning of α or β (α = 0.2 and β = 0.2 are already established as optimal in the paper); use a hyperparameter-analysis workflow instead. The dataset is M3CoT or another benchmark whose per-category structure (NAT/TXT/SOC, G1–6) does not apply. Reproduce and assemble a controlled baseline-vs-ablation comparison table (e.g., VSSD's Table 3: attention-guided perturbed-image (PI) vs black-image (BKG) settings) reporting two-stage multimodal CoT metrics — rationale RougeL and answer accuracy — for Base and Large model variants on ScienceQA. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11463006

skills.search_text: benchmark-evaluation-reproduction Use when a paper reports paired statistical tests (Δ, p-value, Cohen's d) over per-query benchmark scores and you must independently recompute and validate them from raw per-query outputs. The systems being compared were evaluated on different query sets, so per-query scores cannot be joined on query ID for a paired test. The reported statistic is an unpaired two-sample comparison or a correlation, not a paired mean difference over per-query scores. skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-dataset benchmarking against external baselines in Tables 1–2 rather than internal ablation across component removals The model does not consume image-text meme pairs (e.g., text-only classification), since Long-CLIP/LLaVA/GPT-4-based multi-CoT evaluation assumes multimodal memes Input memes require processing beyond standard CLIP's 20-token limit but Long-CLIP (248-token context) is not available, making the ablation condition unreproducible

skills.summary: Parses Groff-format man pages of command-line programs into structured records (program name, description, synopsis, option descriptions) that downstream LLM modules consume for constraint extraction. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input documentation is not in Groff/man-page format (e.g., HTML-only docs, PDFs, or texinfo) — the keyword matching targets Groff macros like .TH, .SH, .TP The goal is direct fuzzing of binaries without documentation-based constraint extraction — downstream stages (prediction, assembly, fuzzing) would be unnecessary overhead

When the question is only about final-output (C1) sanitization quality — the skill's core value is the C1 vs C2 audit gap, so an output-only audit will miss the inter-agent violations this skill targets When the system under test is not a coordinator-worker multi-agent pipeline (or single-agent baseline) instrumented with the agentleak SDK on CrewAI/LangGraph integrations When offline/deterministic evaluation is required — runs depend on live LLM API calls via OpenRouter and HYBRID detection (~200ms latency per check) Sets up and benchmarks single-agent vs multi-agent coordinator-worker LLM configurations in the AgentLeak harness to quantify privacy leakage on final outputs (C1) versus internal inter-agent channels (C2). It exists because output-only audits miss a large fraction of violations that occur on internal channels. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/access.2026.3704541
skills.summary: Sets up and benchmarks single-agent vs multi-agent coordinator-worker LLM configurations in the AgentLeak harness to quantify privacy leakage on final outputs (C1) versus internal inter-agent channels (C2). It exists because output-only audits miss a large fraction of violations that occur on internal channels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is only about final-output (C1) sanitization quality — the skill's core value is the C1 vs C2 audit gap, so an output-only audit will miss the inter-agent violations this skill targets When the system under test is not a coordinator-worker multi-agent pipeline (or single-agent baseline) instrumented with the agentleak SDK on CrewAI/LangGraph integrations When offline/deterministic evaluation is required — runs depend on live LLM API calls via OpenRouter and HYBRID detection (~200ms latency per check)

skills.summary: Implements Visual Saliency-guided Steering Distillation (VSSD), which distills large multimodal LLM reasoning into small models for multimodal chain-of-thought tasks by injecting SVD-extracted steering vectors from saliency-perturbed images into intermediate decoder layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task targets broader multimodal reasoning beyond small multimodal CoT settings — the paper explicitly defers this to future work An adaptive, input-dependent steering-vector extraction is required — current extraction is not adaptive and adaptive extraction is deferred to future work No paired question-image data or attention maps from a larger MLLM are available to generate the negatively perturbed semantic samples

skills.description: Use when interpreting harmful memes requires background knowledge and multi-perspective reasoning: for each meme M = {I, T}, generate paired benign/hateful CoT chains to feed a downstream fusion-and-alignment model.
skills.name: multimodal-chain-of-thought-prompting
skills.search_text: multimodal-chain-of-thought-prompting Use when interpreting harmful memes requires background knowledge and multi-perspective reasoning: for each meme M = {I, T}, generate paired benign/hateful CoT chains to feed a downstream fusion-and-alignment model. The downstream encoder is standard CLIP rather than Long-CLIP: CoT sequences of ~150 words exceed the ~20-token comfort zone of standard CLIP, so shortening or replacing chains is required first (the paper lists chain-shortening as future work). The task is plain image classification without meme text or implicit/hateful semantics — the skill's value comes from explaining image-text relations via benign/hateful comparative reasoning. http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 Generates multiple benign and hateful chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning chains per meme with an MLLM (LLaVA-1.5-7B or GPT-4) so that comparative multi-CoT evidence, rather than a single unreliable chain, grounds harmful meme detection. This is the Multi-CoT Generation phase (Section 3.1) of the EVL-MCoT framework. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-981-95-3349-7_31
skills.summary: Generates multiple benign and hateful chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning chains per meme with an MLLM (LLaVA-1.5-7B or GPT-4) so that comparative multi-CoT evidence, rather than a single unreliable chain, grounds harmful meme detection. This is the Multi-CoT Generation phase (Section 3.1) of the EVL-MCoT framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream encoder is standard CLIP rather than Long-CLIP: CoT sequences of ~150 words exceed the ~20-token comfort zone of standard CLIP, so shortening or replacing chains is required first (the paper lists chain-shortening as future work). The task is plain image classification without meme text or implicit/hateful semantics — the skill's value comes from explaining image-text relations via benign/hateful comparative reasoning.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or adapting the supervised OCR&UIE baseline on scanned/embedded document images (e.g., Chinese bidding certificates) where per-type extraction quality is benchmarked against F1-score and normalized edit distance (NED).
skills.name: ocr-detection-recognition-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: ocr-detection-recognition-fine-tuning Use when reproducing or adapting the supervised OCR&UIE baseline on scanned/embedded document images (e.g., Chinese bidding certificates) where per-type extraction quality is benchmarked against F1-score and normalized edit distance (NED). The goal is zero-shot or minimally supervised extraction — the paper's classification-guided LVLM approach (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) reaches 86.43% F1 / 0.90 NED without task-specific training, so use OCR fine-tuning only when a supervised baseline is explicitly required. Input images are public benchmarks like SROIE or SCID, which the authors note are limited in document variety, layout complexity, and entity types relative to the multi-type bidding data this pipeline targets. No annotated samples exist at all — the pipeline still requires PaddleLabel/Doccano labels for the OCR and per-type UIE stages. Fine-tunes a supervised two-stage OCR pipeline (DB text detection + CRNN recognition) from a pre-trained PaddleOCR model on Chinese document images, as the supervised baseline for visually rich information extraction (VIE) on a real-world bidding dataset with 16 certificate types. agentic-ai/v1 10.1038/s41598-026-49319-z
skills.summary: Fine-tunes a supervised two-stage OCR pipeline (DB text detection + CRNN recognition) from a pre-trained PaddleOCR model on Chinese document images, as the supervised baseline for visually rich information extraction (VIE) on a real-world bidding dataset with 16 certificate types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is zero-shot or minimally supervised extraction — the paper's classification-guided LVLM approach (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) reaches 86.43% F1 / 0.90 NED without task-specific training, so use OCR fine-tuning only when a supervised baseline is explicitly required. Input images are public benchmarks like SROIE or SCID, which the authors note are limited in document variety, layout complexity, and entity types relative to the multi-type bidding data this pipeline targets. No annotated samples exist at all — the pipeline still requires PaddleLabel/Doccano labels for the OCR and per-type UIE stages.

skills.description: Use when building a curated short-video corpus (≤60 s YouTube-sourced clips) and you need to screen candidate videos for motion blur or static segments as part of multimodal quality filtering before temporal annotation.
skills.name: optical-flow-motion-variance-analysis
skills.search_text: optical-flow-motion-variance-analysis Use when building a curated short-video corpus (≤60 s YouTube-sourced clips) and you need to screen candidate videos for motion blur or static segments as part of multimodal quality filtering before temporal annotation. The input is not video (e.g., already-extracted captions, QA pairs, or metadata tables) — the other StreamingCoT quality filters (lexical density constraints, aesthetic scoring ≥7/10, social validation >5,000 interactions) apply instead. The videos are long-form streams where per-window exclusion of whole files is inappropriate; this filter was designed to exclude entire ≤60 s candidate clips, not to trim segments within longer recordings. The corpus explicitly requires static or slow footage (e.g., time-lapse or slideshow benchmarks); this filter would systematically exclude such content by design. A motion-dynamics screening filter from the StreamingCoT construction pipeline that computes dense frame-to-frame optical flow variance over 30-second windows to exclude videos with excessive motion blur (≥15% high-variance frames) or near-static content (≥85% static occupancy) before dataset annotation. agentic-ai/v1 10.1145/3746027.3758311
skills.summary: A motion-dynamics screening filter from the StreamingCoT construction pipeline that computes dense frame-to-frame optical flow variance over 30-second windows to exclude videos with excessive motion blur (≥15% high-variance frames) or near-static content (≥85% static occupancy) before dataset annotation.

skills.summary: A numerical reconciliation skill that recomputes a stated percentage (e.g., a claimed compute share) from its two reported raw figures and checks whether the quotient is consistent with the claim, quantifying the absolute and relative discrepancy. skills.search_text: perturbation-strategy-ablation-analysis Use when benchmarking a visual jailbreak method whose adversarial image perturbation module exposes multiple perturbation-strategy conditions (Full/Patch/Grid) and you must quantify how strategy choice affects both ASR and MIFR. The analysis goal is a single-condition attack run and no strategy comparison is needed (Full, Patch, and Grid runs are redundant). The method under study has no image perturbation module or does not define Full/Patch/Grid perturbation-strategy conditions. skills.description: Use when building a physics-informed neural network for digital twin modeling and you need to embed governing PDEs and boundary conditions into the loss alongside observed measurement data.
skills.name: pinn-composite-loss-formulation
skills.search_text: pinn-composite-loss-formulation Use when building a physics-informed neural network for digital twin modeling and you need to embed governing PDEs and boundary conditions into the loss alongside observed measurement data. The model is a purely data-driven regressor trained only on measurements, with no governing PDE or boundary conditions to enforce (e.g., mirroring-stage simulator building rather than modeling the physical twin). The physical system is handled by a traditional numerical solver, neural operator, or foundation model rather than a PINN trained with a PDE-residual loss term. Reconstructs the physics-informed neural network (PINN) training objective from Section 3.1.2 of arXiv:2601.01321 as a composite loss L_PINN = lambda_data*L_data + lambda_PDE*(L_physics + L_boundary), implemented in PyTorch, so that physical equations and boundary conditions constrain digital-twin neural network training alongside the data misfit. agentic-ai/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2601.01321
skills.summary: Reconstructs the physics-informed neural network (PINN) training objective from Section 3.1.2 of arXiv:2601.01321 as a composite loss L_PINN = lambda_data*L_data + lambda_PDE*(L_physics + L_boundary), implemented in PyTorch, so that physical equations and boundary conditions constrain digital-twin neural network training alongside the data misfit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is a purely data-driven regressor trained only on measurements, with no governing PDE or boundary conditions to enforce (e.g., mirroring-stage simulator building rather than modeling the physical twin). The physical system is handled by a traditional numerical solver, neural operator, or foundation model rather than a PINN trained with a PDE-residual loss term.

The answer is a free-form response to general-purpose (non-domain) queries where the retrieved pool D∪W is irrelevant or empty — sentences will fail the 0.75 similarity cutoff and no citations can be inserted. You need citations that are absent in baseline standalone LLM systems; this skill only works with an explicit retrievable chunk pool with trackable chunk indices, not with parametric model memory. This is Stage 6 ('Citation Insert') of the AgriIR pipeline, responsible for its high citation quality. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-21324-2_37

skills.search_text: postgres-batched-bulk-indexing Use when a tokenized textual-fact corpus (hundreds of millions of verbalized triples) must be indexed into a persistent prefix tree so next-token queries during constrained generation avoid duplicate facts and stay efficient at scale. The knowledge base is small enough to fit in memory — use the in-memory prefix tree from the 31k-facts knowledge base in try_refactx.ipynb instead of the disk-backed PostgreSQL ingestion pipeline The goal is unconstrained generation or retrieval-augmented QA with a retriever — ReFactX is explicitly positioned as an alternative to pipeline-based solutions with external retrievers Input triples are not verbalizable into natural-language textual facts, since the index is over tokenized verbalized facts, not raw triples Build and persist a disk-backed prefix-tree fact index in PostgreSQL so that constrained-generation over very large knowledge bases (up to 800M Wikidata textual facts) stays scalable: the tree is built in-memory batch by batch because hardware memory limits preclude holding it whole, with subtrees packed via Pickle and a B-Tree index on the Prefix column for fast prefix-match lookups. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-09527-5_16
skills.summary: Build and persist a disk-backed prefix-tree fact index in PostgreSQL so that constrained-generation over very large knowledge bases (up to 800M Wikidata textual facts) stays scalable: the tree is built in-memory batch by batch because hardware memory limits preclude holding it whole, with subtrees packed via Pickle and a B-Tree index on the Prefix column for fast prefix-match lookups.

Observations are already expressed in the vessel frame, so the R^-1 transform is unnecessary or would double-rotate the relative velocity The scenario is not the pursuit-evasion task (e.g. KSPDG Lady-Bandit-Guard or sun-blocking problems), where the pursuer-minus-evader relative velocity is not the relevant augmentation quantity The goal is high-fidelity astrodynamical trajectory analysis rather than prompt augmentation for an LLM agent — use Lambert solvers or orbital propagation instead Augments an LLM agent's observation space for the KSPDG Pursuer-Evader task by computing a normalized prograde vector p = R^-1 (v_p - v_e)/||v_p - v_e||, i.e. the pursuer-minus-evader velocity difference, normalized and rotated from the celestial-body reference frame into the vessel frame, then added to the prompt. agentic-ai/v1 10.1016/j.asr.2025.06.034
skills.summary: Augments an LLM agent's observation space for the KSPDG Pursuer-Evader task by computing a normalized prograde vector p = R^-1 (v_p - v_e)/||v_p - v_e||, i.e. the pursuer-minus-evader velocity difference, normalized and rotated from the celestial-body reference frame into the vessel frame, then added to the prompt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Observations are already expressed in the vessel frame, so the R^-1 transform is unnecessary or would double-rotate the relative velocity The scenario is not the pursuit-evasion task (e.g. KSPDG Lady-Bandit-Guard or sun-blocking problems), where the pursuer-minus-evader relative velocity is not the relevant augmentation quantity The goal is high-fidelity astrodynamical trajectory analysis rather than prompt augmentation for an LLM agent — use Lambert solvers or orbital propagation instead

skills.search_text: prompt-token-masking-in-loss-computation Use when fine-tuning a base model on instruction data with a chat template and you must prevent the loss from back-propagating through prompt tokens (e.g. OLMo-2-0425-1B SFT on HuggingFaceH4/no_robots). Training on full next-token prediction over unstructured corpora (pretraining), where predicting every position including 'prompt-like' text is intended Direct alignment or RL stages (DPO, PPO) where the objective is over full sampled completions rather than supervised teacher forcing Datasets without chat-template formatting where prompt/completion boundaries cannot be reliably located http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A supervised fine-tuning (SFT) technique in which tokens belonging to the formatted prompt (including chat-template role markers) are masked out of the cross-entropy loss via a completion_mask, so the model only learns to predict completion tokens. This is the core loss computation behind the base-model-to-assistant transition demonstrated by the RLHF Book's SFT recipe. agentic-ai/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2504.12501
skills.summary: A supervised fine-tuning (SFT) technique in which tokens belonging to the formatted prompt (including chat-template role markers) are masked out of the cross-entropy loss via a completion_mask, so the model only learns to predict completion tokens. This is the core loss computation behind the base-model-to-assistant transition demonstrated by the RLHF Book's SFT recipe.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training on full next-token prediction over unstructured corpora (pretraining), where predicting every position including 'prompt-like' text is intended Direct alignment or RL stages (DPO, PPO) where the objective is over full sampled completions rather than supervised teacher forcing Datasets without chat-template formatting where prompt/completion boundaries cannot be reliably located

skills.search_text: prompt-variant-benchmarking Use when you must choose a prompt/configuration for an LLM MCQ benchmark, or need to quantify how seed, temperature, and prompt complexity affect run-to-run consistency of GPT-3.5/GPT-4 outputs. The GPT-3.5-optimized configuration is being applied to a different LLM or VLM family — the article notes prompts/settings were optimized only for OpenAI models and reused for others, and generalizability remains uncertain; per-model prompt configuration may be more effective The goal is to improve absolute accuracy rather than measure consistency — the paper found that the most consistent configuration did not necessarily improve accuracy The evaluation target is real-world dynamic interaction, documentation/extraction behavior, or hallucination detection — MCQ accuracy and consistency do not capture these A method for benchmarking prompt variants (e.g., 'Just QA', QA followed by 'are you sure?', open-ended vs. MCQ with/without justification) and model settings (random seed, temperature, max-token) for reproducible LLM evaluation on gastroenterology MCQs, quantifying run-to-run output consistency as well as accuracy. agentic-ai/v1 10.1038/s41746-025-02174-0

skills.search_text: prototype-based-cross-modal-fusion-inference Use when classifying harmful memes (or similar vision-language tasks) from image-text pairs where fine-grained visual-textual alignment is needed and single-chain CoT reasoning is insufficient; inputs are Long-CLIP visual/textual embeddings plus multi-CoT chains. skills.description: Use when you need to explain a CLIP-based retrieval similarity score at the pixel level — e.g. after a composed image retrieval search (reference image φ(I_ref) + text prompt) — by producing a gradient-based heatmap of influential image regions.
skills.name: pytorch-backpropagation-through-vision-transformer
skills.search_text: pytorch-backpropagation-through-vision-transformer Use when you need to explain a CLIP-based retrieval similarity score at the pixel level — e.g. after a composed image retrieval search (reference image φ(I_ref) + text prompt) — by producing a gradient-based heatmap of influential image regions. skills.search_text: rouge-bertscore-generation-evaluation Use when scoring natural-language generations (e.g., ATOMIC tail predictions from T5 variants) against multiple reference tails per head and comparing fine-tuning configurations with automatic text-generation metrics. The target task is not natural-language generation (e.g., classification or QA multiple-choice scoring), where BLEU/ROUGE-style overlap metrics are not the paper's evaluation focus Only a single reference exists per head with no multiple-tail scoring convention, so the max-over-tails instance scoring of the paper does not apply Human-adequacy or semantic-correctness judgments are needed; the paper's automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT) only capture correlation, not correctness guarantees Evaluation protocol for tail-generation (KB completion) outputs from T5-based models: score each generated tail against gold tails with ROUGE, BERTScore, and BLEURT, keeping the highest per-instance score over a head's tails, then rely on ROUGE as the representative metric given the high correlation among the three. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/s10489-024-05660-2
skills.summary: Evaluation protocol for tail-generation (KB completion) outputs from T5-based models: score each generated tail against gold tails with ROUGE, BERTScore, and BLEURT, keeping the highest per-instance score over a head's tails, then rely on ROUGE as the representative metric given the high correlation among the three.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target task is not natural-language generation (e.g., classification or QA multiple-choice scoring), where BLEU/ROUGE-style overlap metrics are not the paper's evaluation focus Only a single reference exists per head with no multiple-tail scoring convention, so the max-over-tails instance scoring of the paper does not apply Human-adequacy or semantic-correctness judgments are needed; the paper's automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT) only capture correlation, not correctness guarantees

skills.description: Use when evaluating sequence-to-sequence generation of commonsense KB tails (or similar multi-reference text generation) where each head has 3+ gold continuations and models fine-tuned with different templates/objectives must be compared.
skills.name: rouge-generation-metric-computation
skills.search_text: rouge-generation-metric-computation Use when evaluating sequence-to-sequence generation of commonsense KB tails (or similar multi-reference text generation) where each head has 3+ gold continuations and models fine-tuned with different templates/objectives must be compared. Evaluating classification-style tasks where output is a single discrete choice (e.g. CommonsenseQA / Open BookQA answer accuracy) rather than free-form generated tails scored against multiple gold references. Comparing non-generative retrieval or embedding-based KB completion methods whose outputs are not tail strings consumable by ROUGE. Settings without multiple gold tails per head (single-reference scoring), where the highest-score-against-gold-tails attribution scheme does not apply. Computes ROUGE scores for free-form generated tail texts in commonsense KB completion (ATOMIC2020 Mask-Filling / Map-Phrasal relations) using MTO-framework T5 checkpoints, attributing each test instance the highest ROUGE against its gold tails. This protocol makes few-shot gains of MTO-aligned templates over the conventional Mapping baseline quantitatively comparable. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/s10489-024-05660-2
skills.summary: Computes ROUGE scores for free-form generated tail texts in commonsense KB completion (ATOMIC2020 Mask-Filling / Map-Phrasal relations) using MTO-framework T5 checkpoints, attributing each test instance the highest ROUGE against its gold tails. This protocol makes few-shot gains of MTO-aligned templates over the conventional Mapping baseline quantitatively comparable.

skills.description: Use when a generated candidate JSON (e.g. Stage 2 hourly weather or Stage 3 hourly consumption) must be checked against its schemas/ JSON schema before acceptance, with failures routed to the council regeneration loop.
skills.name: schema-constraint-validation
skills.search_text: schema-constraint-validation Use when a generated candidate JSON (e.g. Stage 2 hourly weather or Stage 3 hourly consumption) must be checked against its schemas/ JSON schema before acceptance, with failures routed to the council regeneration loop. The input is real measured data (TMY meteorological data for the capital coordinates or CER dataset load measurements) processed outside the LLM generation loop, so there is no LLM candidate to gate. The goal is statistical evaluation of generated profiles against the CER dataset (4232 households) or ablation studies, rather than structural/constraint conformance of a single candidate. No governed council loop exists (no schemas/ files, no CEO arbiter) — a plain one-shot validator cannot implement the REGENERATE_PARTIAL / REGENERATE_FULL semantics this skill assumes. WattCouncil's schema-constraint validation checks each LLM-generated structured JSON (family composition, hourly weather, hourly consumption) against the stage-specific JSON schemas in schemas/ and routes failures through the governed council loop rather than dropping them. It guarantees that only schema-conforming candidates that survive auditor review and a CEO ACCEPT become stage2_hourly_* / stage3_consumption_* outputs. agentic-ai/v1 10.1145/3744256.3812595

skills.summary: A semi-automated evaluation pipeline step that uses GPT-3.5 via the OpenAI Python package and LangChain to map each LLM's free-text MCQ response onto a single scorable option label (A–E or a sentinel NOP, EOP, 2OP, error), enabling automated scoring of benchmark answers.

skills.summary: Serializes the multi-CoT reasoning chains produced by an MLLM (e.g., LLaVA-1.5-7B or GPT-4) for each harmful-meme tuple M = {I, T} into a structured JSON file (multi_cot_chains.), preserving per-meme hateful/benign chains and their n × m comparative pairings for downstream contrastive training in EVL-MCoT.

skills.name: structured-report-generation
skills.search_text: structured-report-generation Use when free-text clinical narratives (e.g., MIMIC-CXR radiology reports) must be converted into structured reports whose sections follow a named clinical protocol (ABCDEF), with verifiable tool-grounded steps instead of a single monolithic LLM call. The report is already structured (e.g., already a JSON/checklist document) — the skill targets unstructured, free-text narratives where checklist organization was lost in dictation The task requires integrating medical images or automated suggestion systems — the article lists these as future work, not implemented A real-time clinical deployment is required — the article notes this depends on model compression and hardware acceleration optimizations not yet achieved http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Generate protocol-compliant structured medical reports from free-text clinical narratives by decomposing the task into a Plan-Act-Observe loop over specialized, verifiable tools (concept extraction, ontology mapping/filtering, protocol categorization, report generation), as instantiated by MedPAO for the ABCDEF chest X-ray protocol on MIMIC-CXR reports. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-06004-4_4
skills.summary: Generate protocol-compliant structured medical reports from free-text clinical narratives by decomposing the task into a Plan-Act-Observe loop over specialized, verifiable tools (concept extraction, ontology mapping/filtering, protocol categorization, report generation), as instantiated by MedPAO for the ABCDEF chest X-ray protocol on MIMIC-CXR reports.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The report is already structured (e.g., already a JSON/checklist document) — the skill targets unstructured, free-text narratives where checklist organization was lost in dictation The task requires integrating medical images or automated suggestion systems — the article lists these as future work, not implemented A real-time clinical deployment is required — the article notes this depends on model compression and hardware acceleration optimizations not yet achieved

skills.when_to_use_negative: The source presents a flat list of techniques without an explicit stage or lifecycle structure — no canonical entities exist to key rows on The goal is bibliometric aggregation or citation counts rather than extracting a paper's own definitional framework The framework stages are ambiguous or renamed across sections, requiring interpretive synthesis rather than verbatim extraction

skills.description: Use when a reference song (e.g., a pop track) is provided with a natural-language request to understand its musical style, extract its accompaniment, and create new music in the same style.
skills.name: style-conditioned-music-generation
skills.search_text: style-conditioned-music-generation Use when a reference song (e.g., a pop track) is provided with a natural-language request to understand its musical style, extract its accompaniment, and create new music in the same style. The task involves only speech or sound understanding (e.g., ASR, speech emotion recognition) with no music generation or style transfer component. FunTTS_mcp_servers, music_mcp_servers, and Audioseparator_mcp_servers have been removed from servers_config.json because local models were not deployed and no API tokens (MD_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN) are configured — the required tools will not be available. The input is already a finished composition request needing only Text2Music/Lyrics2Song without a reference track for style conditioning. skills.summary: An AudioFab workflow that generates a new piece of music in the style of a reference song by chaining Demucs vocal/accompaniment separation, Qwen2-Audio style description of the instrumental track, and DiffRhythm style-conditioned generation.

The input is already a finished composition request needing only Text2Music/Lyrics2Song without a reference track for style conditioning.

skills.description: Use when visualizing CLIP-based composed image retrieval results in 2D: if neighborhoods are grouped by artistic style instead of semantics, apply PCA-based style debiasing, contrastive debiasing, and ICA before fitting UMAP.
skills.name: style-debiased-embedding-projection
skills.search_text: style-debiased-embedding-projection Use when visualizing CLIP-based composed image retrieval results in 2D: if neighborhoods are grouped by artistic style instead of semantics, apply PCA-based style debiasing, contrastive debiasing, and ICA before fitting UMAP. When the goal is metric distance reading (e.g. computing exact similarity values from the 2D layout) — the projection is explicitly qualitative/topological, not metric When embeddings have not been style-debiased: vanilla UMAP on raw CLIP space suffers from style bias, clustering images by artistic style rather than semantic categories When a quick qualitative check of unimodal (text-only or image-only) embeddings suffices — the pipeline targets composed image retrieval, where reference, query, and retrieved images must share one space http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A supervised metric projection pipeline that uses a debiased UMAP approach to place reference images, SEARLE-composed query embeddings, and top-k retrieved images into one shared 2D space, specifically designed to overcome the style bias that makes vanilla UMAP cluster CLIP embeddings by artistic style rather than semantic category. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/pacificvis68791.2026.00041
skills.summary: A supervised metric projection pipeline that uses a debiased UMAP approach to place reference images, SEARLE-composed query embeddings, and top-k retrieved images into one shared 2D space, specifically designed to overcome the style bias that makes vanilla UMAP cluster CLIP embeddings by artistic style rather than semantic category.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is metric distance reading (e.g. computing exact similarity values from the 2D layout) — the projection is explicitly qualitative/topological, not metric When embeddings have not been style-debiased: vanilla UMAP on raw CLIP space suffers from style bias, clustering images by artistic style rather than semantic categories When a quick qualitative check of unimodal (text-only or image-only) embeddings suffices — the pipeline targets composed image retrieval, where reference, query, and retrieved images must share one space

skills.description: Use when CLIP-based embedding projections (e.g., UMAP) cluster images by artistic style rather than semantic categories, and dimensions dominated by stylistic or background variation must be filtered out before visualization.
skills.name: stylistic-vs-semantic-feature-separation
skills.search_text: stylistic-vs-semantic-feature-separation Use when CLIP-based embedding projections (e.g., UMAP) cluster images by artistic style rather than semantic categories, and dimensions dominated by stylistic or background variation must be filtered out before visualization. The input is not a CLIP-style joint image embedding space — the documented failure mode (UMAP clustering images by artistic style) is specific to CLIP-based spaces, not arbitrary feature tables Label supervision is available and supervised alignment is desired — stage (B) Contrastive Debiasing, which aligns embeddings with class prototypes, is the appropriate mechanism instead of heuristic PCA filtering Full original dimensionality is required downstream (e.g., cosine similarity ranking against pre-computed database embeddings) — this stage keeps only the 80 retained principal components http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 PCA-based style debiasing — stage (A) of InfoCIR's three-stage filtering process — for CLIP image embeddings: fit PCA with pca_components=80 on ViT-B/32 ImageNet-R embeddings and retain the components with higher semantic discriminability, so downstream UMAP projections cluster images by semantic category rather than artistic style. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/pacificvis68791.2026.00041
skills.summary: PCA-based style debiasing — stage (A) of InfoCIR's three-stage filtering process — for CLIP image embeddings: fit PCA with pca_components=80 on ViT-B/32 ImageNet-R embeddings and retain the components with higher semantic discriminability, so downstream UMAP projections cluster images by semantic category rather than artistic style.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a CLIP-style joint image embedding space — the documented failure mode (UMAP clustering images by artistic style) is specific to CLIP-based spaces, not arbitrary feature tables Label supervision is available and supervised alignment is desired — stage (B) Contrastive Debiasing, which aligns embeddings with class prototypes, is the appropriate mechanism instead of heuristic PCA filtering Full original dimensionality is required downstream (e.g., cosine similarity ranking against pre-computed database embeddings) — this stage keeps only the 80 retained principal components

skills.description: Use when a complex, multi-faceted user question must be broken into tractable sub-problems before retrieval, e.g. to fan out parallel FAISS + web searches in a configurable RAG pipeline.
skills.name: subquery-decomposition-prompting
skills.search_text: subquery-decomposition-prompting Use when a complex, multi-faceted user question must be broken into tractable sub-problems before retrieval, e.g. to fan out parallel FAISS + web searches in a configurable RAG pipeline. Query is already simple and unambiguous — decomposition adds fan-out cost and can dilute retrieval precision; refinement alone (Stage-1, T=0.1) suffices Framework is deployed in a domain where a single sub-topic covers the information need and 3–5 sub-queries would generate redundant retrievals http://edamontology.org/topic_3379 Stage 2 of the AgriIR six-stage RAG pipeline: a temperature-0.5 LLM call (Gemma3:1B via Ollama) expands a single refined user query into 3–5 sub-queries so that downstream parallel retrieval over FAISS and the web covers complementary facets of the information need. agentic-ai/v1 10.1007/978-3-032-21324-2_37
skills.summary: Stage 2 of the AgriIR six-stage RAG pipeline: a temperature-0.5 LLM call (Gemma3:1B via Ollama) expands a single refined user query into 3–5 sub-queries so that downstream parallel retrieval over FAISS and the web covers complementary facets of the information need.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query is already simple and unambiguous — decomposition adds fan-out cost and can dilute retrieval precision; refinement alone (Stage-1, T=0.1) suffices Framework is deployed in a domain where a single sub-topic covers the information need and 3–5 sub-queries would generate redundant retrievals

skills.description: Use when adapting a retrieval-augmented LLM at inference time to a specialized domain: retrieved passages are available, no labeled training data exists, and the model must self-supervisedly learn to predict retrieved content.
skills.name: suffix-prediction-self-supervised-training
skills.search_text: suffix-prediction-self-supervised-training Use when adapting a retrieval-augmented LLM at inference time to a specialized domain: retrieved passages are available, no labeled training data exists, and the model must self-supervisedly learn to predict retrieved content. The task is full domain retraining with labeled data rather than label-free adaptation at inference time Retrieved passages are too short to yield meaningful prefix-suffix context for suffix prediction You need to reproduce the no-segmentation ablation baseline, which by design skips prefix-suffix splitting and performs next-token prediction on the entire passage http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates self-supervised adaptation signals for test-time RAG adaptation by splitting each retrieved passage into prefix-suffix pairs and training the language model to predict the suffix from the prefix, enabling dynamic parameter updates to the target domain without labeled data. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11464478
skills.summary: Generates self-supervised adaptation signals for test-time RAG adaptation by splitting each retrieved passage into prefix-suffix pairs and training the language model to predict the suffix from the prefix, enabling dynamic parameter updates to the target domain without labeled data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is full domain retraining with labeled data rather than label-free adaptation at inference time Retrieved passages are too short to yield meaningful prefix-suffix context for suffix prediction You need to reproduce the no-segmentation ablation baseline, which by design skips prefix-suffix splitting and performs next-token prediction on the entire passage

skills.description: Use when a pretrained base LLM must be turned into an assistant that follows user questions — i.e., the instruction-tuning stage before reward model training or RL, using a chat-template-formatted SFT dataset.
skills.name: supervised-fine-tuning-with-chat-templates
skills.search_text: supervised-fine-tuning-with-chat-templates Use when a pretrained base LLM must be turned into an assistant that follows user questions — i.e., the instruction-tuning stage before reward model training or RL, using a chat-template-formatted SFT dataset. The task is a later post-training stage (reward model training, rejection sampling, RL, direct alignment) — SFT is only the first step of the pipeline. The input is a preference/reward dataset (e.g., UltraFeedback, HelpSteer2-Preference) rather than prompt-completion instruction data with chat-template turns. You need general next-token LM training without chat structure or completion masking (prompt tokens should not be excluded from the loss). http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Step 1 of the RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) that converts a base model (e.g., allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B) into an instruction-following assistant by training on an instruction dataset (HuggingFaceH4/no_robots) formatted with a chat template, with prompt masking so only completion tokens contribute to the loss. agentic-ai/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2504.12501
skills.summary: Step 1 of the RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) that converts a base model (e.g., allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B) into an instruction-following assistant by training on an instruction dataset (HuggingFaceH4/no_robots) formatted with a chat template, with prompt masking so only completion tokens contribute to the loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a later post-training stage (reward model training, rejection sampling, RL, direct alignment) — SFT is only the first step of the pipeline. The input is a preference/reward dataset (e.g., UltraFeedback, HelpSteer2-Preference) rather than prompt-completion instruction data with chat-template turns. You need general next-token LM training without chat structure or completion masking (prompt tokens should not be excluded from the loss).

The input is raw survey text rather than already-generated topic lists from MALTopic, LDA, and BERTopic — run the topic-modeling pipelines first The goal is purely quantitative scoring (coherence/diversity metrics) rather than qualitative cross-technique topic distinctness analysis The dataset is not survey free-text with structured respondent data, since MALTopic's enrichment agent relies on structured data to enhance textual responses http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Qualitatively characterizes topics extracted from survey free-text responses by cross-technique comparison of MALTopic, LDA, and BERTopic outputs, using sentence-embedding cosine similarity and agglomerative clustering to test whether a multi-agent LLM framework separates semantically distinct themes (e.g., job-market entry challenges vs. job-displacement concerns) that baselines collapse. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/aiiot65859.2025.11105319
skills.summary: Qualitatively characterizes topics extracted from survey free-text responses by cross-technique comparison of MALTopic, LDA, and BERTopic outputs, using sentence-embedding cosine similarity and agglomerative clustering to test whether a multi-agent LLM framework separates semantically distinct themes (e.g., job-market entry challenges vs. job-displacement concerns) that baselines collapse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw survey text rather than already-generated topic lists from MALTopic, LDA, and BERTopic — run the topic-modeling pipelines first The goal is purely quantitative scoring (coherence/diversity metrics) rather than qualitative cross-technique topic distinctness analysis The dataset is not survey free-text with structured respondent data, since MALTopic's enrichment agent relies on structured data to enhance textual responses

skills.description: Use when you need to synthesize symbolic expert trajectories (e.g., via an A* oracle over a grid transition graph) and render them as prompt-action pairs to fine-tune a language model as a next-action predictor.
skills.name: symbolic-to-text-trajectory-prompting
skills.search_text: symbolic-to-text-trajectory-prompting Use when you need to synthesize symbolic expert trajectories (e.g., via an A* oracle over a grid transition graph) and render them as prompt-action pairs to fine-tune a language model as a next-action predictor. Input is not a discrete symbolic planning domain with a deterministic transition graph over grid states and actions You need the downstream RL policy itself (PPO) or the uncertainty blending mechanism (MC dropout, entropy-based blending) rather than trajectory-to-prompt data generation A meaningful admissible heuristic (e.g., Manhattan distance) cannot be defined, making A* oracle synthesis infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 Converts A*-synthesized optimal symbolic state-action trajectories from a MiniGrid transition graph into textual prompts used to fine-tune a BERT-based next-action predictor. skills.summary: Converts A*-synthesized optimal symbolic state-action trajectories from a MiniGrid transition graph into textual prompts used to fine-tune a BERT-based next-action predictor. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a discrete symbolic planning domain with a deterministic transition graph over grid states and actions You need the downstream RL policy itself (PPO) or the uncertainty blending mechanism (MC dropout, entropy-based blending) rather than trajectory-to-prompt data generation A meaningful admissible heuristic (e.g., Manhattan distance) cannot be defined, making A* oracle synthesis infeasible

skills.description: Use when evaluating a personalized-recommendation or meal-planning system but no human study data exist, and you need reproducible synthetic user profiles with randomized goals drawn from a plausible range (e.g., 1500-3500 kcal).
skills.name: synthetic-user-profile-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-user-profile-generation Use when evaluating a personalized-recommendation or meal-planning system but no human study data exist, and you need reproducible synthetic user profiles with randomized goals drawn from a plausible range (e.g., 1500-3500 kcal). Real user dietary data or a human user study is available — measured profiles are preferable to simulated ones The downstream evaluation requires profiles outside the plausible adult daily-intake range (e.g., clinical or pediatric targets below 1500 or above 3500 kcal) The evaluation metric depends on user behavior or adherence dynamics rather than static intake targets and meal compositions A simulation skill for composing realistic synthetic user inputs (e.g., ten daily dietary profiles sampled from a USDA meal pool with randomized calorie/protein/sugar targets) so that systems like NutriGen can be evaluated without running a human user study. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/embc58623.2025.11253879
skills.summary: A simulation skill for composing realistic synthetic user inputs (e.g., ten daily dietary profiles sampled from a USDA meal pool with randomized calorie/protein/sugar targets) so that systems like NutriGen can be evaluated without running a human user study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real user dietary data or a human user study is available — measured profiles are preferable to simulated ones The downstream evaluation requires profiles outside the plausible adult daily-intake range (e.g., clinical or pediatric targets below 1500 or above 3500 kcal) The evaluation metric depends on user behavior or adherence dynamics rather than static intake targets and meal compositions

skills.search_text: tabular-score-aggregation Use when a curated video corpus must be quality-gated by aesthetic score — e.g., short (≤60 s) YouTube-sourced clips needing a 0–10 CLIP+MLP aesthetic score and a ≥7/10 keep/discard decision logged per video in a CSV. The quality gate of interest is a different screening criterion — HD resolution (≥720p), motion dynamics analysis, social validation (>5,000 interactions), or lexical density constraints — rather than aesthetic score. You need dataset assembly or geographic balancing (stratified geographic sampling via the YouTube API) rather than per-video aesthetic scoring and tabular keep/discard logging. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies the StreamingCoT aesthetic-quality gate: each candidate short video is scored with a CLIP+MLP Aesthetic Score Predictor (Open-Sora style) on a 0–10 scale, and per-video scores plus keep/discard decisions are aggregated into a tabular CSV, retaining only videos scoring ≥7/10 to maintain the aesthetic integrity of the dataset. agentic-ai/v1 10.1145/3746027.3758311
skills.summary: Applies the StreamingCoT aesthetic-quality gate: each candidate short video is scored with a CLIP+MLP Aesthetic Score Predictor (Open-Sora style) on a 0–10 scale, and per-video scores plus keep/discard decisions are aggregated into a tabular CSV, retaining only videos scoring ≥7/10 to maintain the aesthetic integrity of the dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The corpus has already passed aesthetic screening and only needs downstream pipeline stages (hierarchical captioning, dynamic QA generation, multimodal CoT synthesis, iterative validation). skills.search_text: temperature-controlled-answer-synthesis Use when a retrieval-augmented pipeline has already collected parallel evidence corpora (local vector search D and web results W) and needs a deterministic, low-temperature final answer synthesis step in a resource-constrained, domain-specific setting. skills.description: Use when a RAG system faces distribution shifts or domain-specific dependencies in specialized domains and you need to adapt the LLM during inference without labeled data or model retraining.
skills.name: test-time-adaptation-for-retrieval-augmented-generation
skills.search_text: test-time-adaptation-for-retrieval-augmented-generation Use when a RAG system faces distribution shifts or domain-specific dependencies in specialized domains and you need to adapt the LLM during inference without labeled data or model retraining. The task requires exact-match string scoring rather than semantic-equivalence judgment, since TTARAG's evaluation protocol relies on LLM-as-a-judge semantic equivalence (98% agreement with human annotators on 100 sampled examples). Retrieved passages fall below the configured minimum length threshold, leaving insufficient context for meaningful prefix-suffix adaptation. You need to answer whether segmentation into prefix-suffix pairs matters — in that case run the ablation that performs next-token prediction on the entire passage without prefix-suffix splitting instead of the full method. http://edamontology.org/topic_3377 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 TTARAG dynamically updates a language model's parameters at inference time using self-supervised learning signals generated by splitting retrieved passages into prefix-suffix pairs and training the model to predict the suffix from the prefix, improving RAG performance in specialized domains without new labeled data or retraining. agentic-ai/v1 10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11464478
skills.summary: TTARAG dynamically updates a language model's parameters at inference time using self-supervised learning signals generated by splitting retrieved passages into prefix-suffix pairs and training the model to predict the suffix from the prefix, improving RAG performance in specialized domains without new labeled data or retraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires exact-match string scoring rather than semantic-equivalence judgment, since TTARAG's evaluation protocol relies on LLM-as-a-judge semantic equivalence (98% agreement with human annotators on 100 sampled examples). Retrieved passages fall below the configured minimum length threshold, leaving insufficient context for meaningful prefix-suffix adaptation. You need to answer whether segmentation into prefix-suffix pairs matters — in that case run the ablation that performs next-token prediction on the entire passage without prefix-suffix splitting instead of the full method.

skills.summary: A procedure for sweeping test-time adaptation (TTARAG) hyperparameters—learning rate (1e-6 to 1e-5) and number of prefix-suffix adaptation pairs (1–5)—over the CRAG benchmark to locate the configuration that maximizes LLM-judged question-answering accuracy.

skills.search_text: threshold-based-annotation-acceptance Use when a generated image-question-answer-grounding draft must be automatically accepted or rejected based on verifier scores, or when selecting the iteration from a multi-round refinement loop against a score threshold. The environment is a single-agent setting or a non-sequential joint-update MARL method (e.g. MAPPO-style simultaneous updates), where the exponential advantage-variance growth with agent position does not arise. Variance growth is not the diagnosis — the article notes HATRPO is less susceptible to high variance than HAPPO because training and trust region setups also mitigate variance, so clipping may be unnecessary there. skills.name: trust-region-surrogate-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: trust-region-surrogate-loss-implementation Use when a sequential-update trust-region MARL trainer (HAPPO/HATRPO with independent actors) shows unstable convergence or exponentially growing advantage-estimator variance as agent count increases, and you need a low-variance clipped replacement for the unclipped importance ratio in the actor. skills.summary: Implement the clipped sequential trust-region surrogate loss (clip-HAPPO and clip-HATRPO) as a drop-in HARL actor update that wraps the joint importance ratio in min(R, 1), bounding the advantage-estimator variance by epsilon squared instead of letting it grow exponentially with the number of agents.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The environment/training setup already keeps advantage-estimate variance low (the paper notes HATRPO is less susceptible to high variance than HAPPO, and the fixed threshold of 1 may be pessimistic in less severe settings). skills.summary: Models a durable-step workflow as a typed event stream (dispatch, external commitment, acknowledgment, durable transition) with injectable crash points, so that recovery fault injection can tie a duplicate-effect failure to a named kill point and a declared invariant rather than to an unexplained crash.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The workflow makes no external commitments or durable effects, so there is no duplicate-effect invariant to violate and the sweep has nothing meaningful to expose You are evaluating raw model capability on static benchmarks (e.g. code generation scores) rather than system-level recovery behavior around the model The recovery adapter already implements reconciliation/idempotency keys and you only need functional testing — the negative-control comparison is then unnecessary overhead

skills.search_text: zero-shot-empathy-score-prediction Use when you need to benchmark how well a large language model (e.g., GPT-4, Llama 3 70B) predicts per-instance empathy scores without any fine-tuning, and to test whether a scale-aware prompt beats a plain prompt.
